interpretation: Metric/reference smoothing is small in the canonical median: oracle_ratio is about 0.981.
Most canonical shortening remains after replacing the sampled reference with the oracle: plr_oracle is about 0.916.
A radial magnitude bias exists even when direction error is below 20 degrees: median speed_ratio is about 0.932 and speed/along bias is negative.
Direction ambiguity amplifies the effect: the high-direction-error tail has median speed_ratio about 0.019.
The near-zero median train/test speed-ratio gap argues against dropout or train/eval mode as the primary explanation.
Target and loss comparisons remain descriptive because the formal matrix does not randomize those factors.
next_interventions: Hold architecture, data, seed and budget fixed; compare vector MSE with a magnitude-plus-direction loss.
Hold architecture and loss fixed; compare avg_velocity with velocity_at_end on the same recordings.
Report radial, directional and total velocity errors together; accept a mechanism only if ATE and 10-second RTE do not worsen.
